# Yundera/AppStore — Nextcloud

**Audit date:** 2026-08-01 · **Store version:** `nextcloud:33.0.3` · **Compose sha:** `b876aaf1749bde79873136f73e796adbcc0b65bd` (commit `0f5955e3e2`, 2026-07-10) · **Ref:** `main` · **Depth:** full · **Scope:** n-a (no `compose_base`)

## Headline

**ERRORED · top severity Minor · risk score 3**

The static leaf ran to completion. The functional leaf could **not** run: no demo PCS instance qualified. Per the binding Functional Review Protocol amendment of 2026-07-17 (rules 2 and 4), only a `✅ Ready` instance may be used, and on the Demo Management board both pool instances read `❌ Error`. This is an **infra** condition and explicitly **not** a fault of the app — the audit should be retried once a demo host is Ready. Because mandatory phases C/D/E/F/G could not be exercised, orchestrator Amendment B4 forbids `compliant`; the result is `errored` (retry), not a verdict about Nextcloud.

## Functionality (Functional leaf — `7HxjTwe63H`) — NOT RUN

**Demo host selected: none.** Rule 6 of the 2026-07-17 amendment requires naming the host used; since none qualified, the board state at audit time is recorded instead.

| Instance | Status | Time Remaining | Last Error | Usable? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `demostaging1.inojob.com` | ❌ Error | 24.0h | Request failed with status code 404 | **No** — not `✅ Ready` (rule 2). Live probe of `https://demostaging1.inojob.com/` returned **HTTP 502** |
| `demostaging2.inojob.com` | ❌ Error | 16.0h | Request failed with status code 404 | **No** — not `✅ Ready` (rule 2). Root probe returns HTTP 200, but the board reports the instance as errored, and it is concurrently held by another run (`functional-ClaudeCodeRoot-audit2` context) |

The board was read twice — initial load and a full reload — in a fresh isolated context `functional-Nextcloud-audit`; both reads were byte-for-byte identical. `🧹 Trigger Cleanup` was **not** clicked on either card, per rule 5. Because neither instance shows `✅ Ready`, rule 3's *most Time Remaining, must exceed 1h* tie-break never applies and rule 4 fires: `no-demo-available`.

Using `demostaging2` on the strength of its HTTP 200 was considered and deliberately rejected: an instance answering on the front door while its provisioning state is errored is exactly the silent-install-failure mode the amendment was written to prevent, and proceeding would have produced a false negative recorded against the app.

| Phase | Result | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A — Session | `errored` | no-demo-available; no qualifying host to log into |
| C — Fresh install | `errored` | not reachable — **install duration not measured** |
| D — Discover app URL | `errored` | not reachable |
| E8 — Works immediately | `errored` | not reachable |
| E9 — Auth gate | `errored` | not reachable — a login gate is present in the compose but was **not** exercised live |
| E10 — Clean boot | `errored` | not reachable — no console/network evidence collected |
| F — Zero-config usability | `errored` | not reachable |
| G — Data persistence (real uninstall-keep-data → reinstall) | `errored` | not reachable — persistence is mandatory and remains **unverified live**. The static persistence check passed, which is explicitly *not* a substitute for the reinstall |
| G′ — Migration | `n-a` | no `PRIOR_VERSION` supplied (an audit runs a single current version) — the one input-forced `n-a` the protocol permits |

No phase was skipped by choice. Every `errored` above is the infra condition of orchestrator Amendment E — *infra genuinely blocked a phase → ERRORED, retry; the app is not blamed* — and not the agent-skip protocol violation.

## Cleanup

**Nothing to uninstall.** No install was attempted on either host, so no residue exists. The audit's browser page was closed; the two pre-existing pages belonging to the concurrent `functional-ClaudeCodeRoot-audit2` run were left untouched. Both demo instances are exactly as found.

## Verdict rationale

The static half alone would grade **non-compliant · Minor · risk score 3** (three Minor fails, no Critical, no Major). It cannot be reported as the verdict, because at `depth=full` a missing mandatory functional phase can never yield `compliant`, and Amendment B4 routes any errored mandatory phase to **ERRORED (retry)** rather than to a verdict about the app. The three Minor findings are real and actionable today; the functional standing of Nextcloud is simply unknown from this run.

## Retry guidance

Re-run at `depth=full` once the Demo Management board shows a `✅ Ready` instance with more than 1h remaining. The static half needs no re-work unless the compose changes. The three Minor fixes — pin `alpine`, ship a distinct thumbnail, raise the `redis`/`cron` cpu_shares tiers — can be raised independently of the retry.
